chain.label: Wing certificated to a static-strength-only standard, with no fatigue analysis or safe operating life established
chain.trigger: No requirements for a fatigue analysis existed at the time the G-73T was originally certificated as a G-73

chain.label: Corrosion throughout the wing box from decades of saltwater operation, including around the right wing fuel sump drain
chain.trigger: corrosion was observed in many locations throughout the airplane's structure, with some areas showing significant pitting and thinning

chain.label: Right rear Z-stringer fatigue-fractured at the WS 34 slosh hole years before the accident
chain.trigger: the airplane's right rear Z-stringer likely fractured first ... had been fractured for some time, most likely years, before the accident

caused_by.evidence: without a fatigue analysis, there was no existing information for the safe operating life of the G-73T wing structure that could have been used as the basis for inspection and retirement requirements

chain.label: Load shed from the broken Z-stringer to the lower skin and then to the rear spar lower spar cap, driving a 16-inch skin crack and rapid spar-cap fatigue
chain.trigger: the high stresses were most likely a result of the shedding of load from the fatigue-fractured and cracked rear Z-stringer and lower skin

caused_by.evidence: the right rear Z-stringer on the accident airplane was broken, causing the load to shed to the skin and leading to fatigue of the skin emanating from a fastener hole adjacent to the fracture
The aft segment of the crack initiated from an area of corrosion and missing skin material around the fuel sump drain near right WS 34

chain.label: Repetitive fuel leaks at the right wing root and dry bay in the months before the accident
chain.trigger: the repetitive fuel leaks near the area where the accident airplane's right wing separated from the fuselage were indicators of structural damage inside the right wing

caused_by.evidence: Because the wing skin and other wing box structures make up the wing fuel tanks, wing fuel leaks can be indicative of discrepancies with the wing box structure

chain.label: Company maintenance program failed to identify and properly repair the cracking — sanding, stop drills, undocumented doublers, sealant-only leak fixes, no repair threshold
chain.trigger: many of the repairs were ineffective in that they did not properly restore the load-carrying capability of the wing structure

caused_by.evidence: Continued crack growth from a stop drill hole is indicative of an underlying structural problem that was not properly addressed in previous maintenance actions
the company's evaluation of the recurring leaks was inadequate because it failed to recognize that the leaks were repeated indicators of structural damage inside the right wing

chain.label: FAA oversight failed to detect and correct the deficiencies in the company's maintenance program
chain.trigger: the failure of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to detect and correct deficiencies in the company's maintenance program

caused_by.evidence: no evidence indicated that the PMI investigated the cause of the repetitive fuel leaks or discussed these issues with company management
these activities did not result in the detection and correction of the systemic deficiencies in the maintenance program that led to this accident

chain.label: Right wing failed and separated from the fuselage at WS 34 shortly after takeoff
chain.trigger: the right wing separated from the airplane at WS 34 while the airplane was operated within its certificated design envelope

caused_by.evidence: the fatigue cracks grew to their critical crack length and the remaining wing structure could no longer sustain the applied loads
the failure of the Chalk's Ocean Airways maintenance program to identify and properly repair fatigue cracks in the right wing
the FAA's failure to identify the inadequacy of the Chalk's Ocean Airways maintenance program was causal to the accident

chain.label: Right wing fuel tank breached, producing an in-flight fire and fireball
chain.trigger: smoke or fire came from the wing or a fireball in the sky

caused_by.evidence: The fire damage to the fuselage and empennage was a result of the failure of the right wing and the subsequent breach in the wing fuel tank

chain.label: Airplane rendered uncontrollable with the right wing separated
chain.trigger: the right wing separated from the airplane at WS 34 ... rendering the airplane uncontrollable

caused_by.evidence: there was nothing that the crew could have done to regain control of the airplane after the in-flight separation of the right wing

chain.label: Airplane descended nose-down and crashed into the shipping channel adjacent to the Port of Miami
chain.trigger: crashed into a shipping channel adjacent to the Port of Miami, Florida, shortly after takeoff

caused_by.evidence: the airplane subsequently descended into the water

chain.label: All 20 people aboard killed by multiple blunt force injuries
chain.trigger: All 20 people aboard the airplane were killed, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces

caused_by.evidence: the main pathologic findings for each occupant were multiple blunt force injuries
